title.tagline: Fifteen years, fifty thousand dollars and one idea. How far can you take it?
title.confirmBody: {{company}} will be closed for good. This can't be undone.

ruleError.eventPending: Respond to this month's event first.
ruleError.actionPoints: You're out of moves this month.
ruleError.cash: You can't afford that right now.
ruleError.cooldown: You did that recently. Give it time.
ruleError.once: You can only do that once.
ruleError.noOptions: There's nothing to choose from yet.
ruleError.noEventPending: There's no event to respond to.

stat.hint: Shows history and what moves it.

cash.name: Cash
cash.explainer: Money in the bank. When it runs out, so does the company, unless someone gives you more.
cash.drivers: Revenue adds to it every month. Salaries, offices, tools, servers and marketing take from it. Funding rounds, loans and grants top it up.

users.name: Users
users.explainer: People actively using the product. They are the base of your revenue and, in most markets, your valuation.
users.drivers: Quality and reputation bring people in for free. Marketing buys them. Bugs, high prices and weak quality make them leave, and users you paid for with a weak product leave fastest.

quality.name: Quality
quality.explainer: How good the product feels, out of 100. It drifts towards what you've actually built.
quality.drivers: Shipped features and designers raise it. Bugs and tech debt drag it down. It changes slowly, so problems and fixes take a few months to show.

morale.name: Morale
morale.explainer: How the team feels, out of 100. Unhappy people work slower and leave.
morale.drivers: Burnout, fear about runway and layoffs pull it down. Offsites, good policies, people managers and wins lift it.

reputation.name: Reputation
reputation.explainer: What the outside world thinks of you, out of 100. It affects growth, hiring and how investors value you.
reputation.drivers: Good press, a good product and decent behaviour build it. Scandals, bad launches and layoffs cost it, and it takes a long time to earn back.

turn.confirmBody: Unused moves don't carry over. End the month anyway?

feed.summaryA11y: Month closed. {{users}} users, {{mrr}} monthly revenue, {{cash}} in the bank.

event.because: This is happening because you {{cause}} in month {{month}}.

picker.fairPrice: Most of the market charges around {{price}}.
picker.budgetHint: Currently {{current}} a month. Paid users stay only if the product is good.
picker.moveSlider: Drag the slider to choose a new amount.

product.roadmapEmpty: Nothing on the roadmap. Engineering is fixing bugs and paying down debt in the meantime.
product.noEngineers: Nobody here can build software yet. Hire an engineer or find a technical co-founder.
product.notReadyShort: Ship the first version to launch

people.noTeam: It's just the founders for now.
people.noCandidatesBody: Open a role to start interviewing. Candidates wait about two months before taking other offers.
people.noPolicies: No policies yet. The culture is whatever happens.

money.noRounds: No outside money yet. Everything so far is yours.

world.shadyTitle: Things a reasonable founder wouldn't do
world.shadyBody: They pay off now. The bill arrives later, and you won't know when.

rivalMood.calm: Busy with their own problems. For now.
rivalMood.watching: Watching you closely. They've started hiring for your roles.
rivalMood.circling: Copying your features and calling your customers.
rivalMood.attacking: Openly coming for your market, with a much bigger budget.

cofounder.cold: Barely speaking to you. Updating their CV in the open.
cofounder.wary: Doing the work, keeping their thoughts to themselves.
cofounder.warm: In it with you. Covers for you when you're stretched.
cofounder.close: Your other half in this. Would take a bullet, or at least a board meeting.

investor.cold: Margot has stopped returning calls the same day.
investor.wary: Margot is polite, attentive and taking notes.
investor.warm: Margot makes introductions without being asked.
investor.close: Margot defends you in rooms you aren't in.

rival.cold: Brexton has made beating you personal.
rival.wary: Brexton sees you as competition, nothing more.
rival.warm: Grudging respect. Brexton likes your posts, occasionally.
rival.close: Brexton has floated the word "partnership". Carefully.

journalist.wary: Dana will take your call, and check every word you say.
journalist.warm: Dana trusts you to be straight with her.
journalist.close: Dana gives you a heads-up before stories run.

empty.all: Nothing has happened yet. Give it a month.
empty.consequence: Nothing has come back to bite you. Yet.

negotiation.opening: {{investor}} slides a term sheet across the table and waits.

reaction.insulted: {{investor}} laughs, then realises you're serious. The room gets colder.
reaction.cool: {{investor}} says they'll "need to think about that", which means no.
reaction.interested: {{investor}} is interested, but counters with terms of their own.
reaction.eager: {{investor}} reaches for a pen before you finish the sentence.

negotiation.pushSeat: Ask them to drop the board seat
negotiation.implied: That values the company at {{pre}} before the money. You'd own {{after}} after.
negotiation.closedBody: {{equity}} of the company at a {{pre}} pre-money valuation. The money is in the bank.

ending.article: {{founder}} started out as {{who}} with an idea in {{market}}. Over {{months}} months the company grew to {{team}} people, peaked at {{users}} users and raised {{raised}} along the way.

new.backgroundBody: Your background shapes what comes easily and what doesn't.
new.backgroundNote: Every background can win. They just lose in different ways.
new.marketBody: Each market grows, pays and fails differently.
new.cofounderBody: A co-founder doubles your capacity and halves your arguments with yourself. They also own a lot of the company.
new.soloBody: Keep all the equity and all the work.
new.nameBody: Names matter less than you think. Change your mind about that later, at great expense.

settings.title: Settings
settings.hapticsBody: Feel turn ends, closed deals and disasters.
settings.confirmBody: Asks first when you still have moves left.
settings.abandonBody: The run ends now and gets a front page of its own. You keep your shares, for what they're worth.
settings.aboutBody: Runway is a game about building a company. Every person and company in it is made up, including the ones that sound familiar.

stage.title: You're a {{stage}} now

stage.multiple: Investors now value you at {{value}}× yearly revenue
stage.next: Next stop: {{stage}}. See the Company tab for what it takes.
